title: Mechanistic Insights into ComC Peptide Recognition by the Peptidase Domain of ComA in Streptococcus mutans for Quorum Sensing: A Computational Study.
authors: Siddique, Mohd Ayaz; Dey, Anuvab; Satpati, Priyadarshi
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该文通过计算模拟研究ComA肽酶结构域与ComC底物肽的识别与切割机制，属于蛋白质-肽互作而非典型TF-DNA体系，但分子动力学与结合自由能方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: In Streptococcus mutans, the recognition and cleavage of a 46-residue precursor peptide known as ComC by the peptidase (PEP) domain of the ComA protein trigger quorum-sensing-mediated biofilm formation, which is a key factor in dental caries. The mechanism behind the high fidelity of ComC processing by the PEP domain remains unclear primarily due to the lack of structural characterization of the ComC:PEP complex. We present a model of the precatalytic complex where a truncated 18-residue ComC peptide is bound to the PEP. In this model, a protonated histidine residue at the active site stabilizes the complex. Additionally, the conserved residues of the peptide, F11 and L19, are situated in the hydrophobic cleft of the protein, providing a plausible explanation for their evolutionary conservation. Using the 18-ComC:PEP complex as a template, we quantitatively assessed the changes in PEP binding affinity (DeltaDeltaG) resulting from alanine mutations at various hydrophobic residues within the 18-ComC peptide. Our findings demonstrate that the energetics of peptide-protein interactions significantly varies based on the location of the alanine mutations. The PEP protein showed strong selectivity against alanine substitutions at conserved positions in 18-ComC, with a DeltaDeltaG of approximately 2.5 kcal/mol, supporting previous kinetic experiments. The simulations also identified three weakly selective positions (DeltaDeltaG < 0.5 kcal/mol) within the 18-ComC that could be targeted for future substrate-based peptide inhibitor design. The alanine substitution in the Gly-Gly motif present before the cleavage site in 18-ComC disrupted the precatalytic state by preventing the accommodation of a methyl group within the PEP protein. The simulations demonstrate the importance of the Gly-Gly signal sequence for ComA recognition and cleavage in experimental assays. Simulations with the postcatalytic complex indicated that deprotonation of the active site histidine can act as a switch for product release. This study connects thermodynamics with the structures of the pre- and postcatalytic complex, clarifying previous experimental results and emphasizing the design of 18-ComC-based peptide inhibitors for PEP in S. mutans.
abstract_zh: 在变形链球菌（Streptococcus mutans）中，由ComA蛋白的肽酶（PEP）结构域识别并切割一个46残基前体肽ComC，触发群体感应介导的生物膜形成，这是龋齿的关键因素。PEP结构域对ComC加工高保真性的机制仍不清楚，主要原因是缺乏ComC:PEP复合物的结构表征。我们提出了一个预催化复合物模型，其中截短的18残基ComC肽与PEP结合。在该模型中，活性位点的一个质子化组氨酸残基稳定了复合物。此外，肽的保守残基F11和L19位于蛋白质的疏水裂隙中，为其进化保守性提供了合理解释。以18-ComC:PEP复合物为模板，我们定量评估了18-ComC肽内不同疏水残基丙氨酸突变引起的PEP结合亲和力变化（DeltaDeltaG）。我们的发现表明，肽-蛋白质相互作用的能量学显著依赖于丙氨酸突变的位置。PEP蛋白对18-ComC中保守位置的丙氨酸替换表现出强选择性，DeltaDeltaG约为2.5 kcal/mol，支持了先前的动力学实验。模拟还识别出18-ComC内三个弱选择性位置（DeltaDeltaG < 0.5 kcal/mol），这些位置可作为未来基于底物的肽抑制剂设计的靶点。18-ComC中切割位点前存在的Gly-Gly基序的丙氨酸替换，通过阻止甲基基团在PEP蛋白内的容纳，破坏了预催化状态。模拟证明了Gly-Gly信号序列在实验测定中对ComA识别和切割的重要性。后催化复合物的模拟表明，活性位点组氨酸的去质子化可作为产物释放的开关。本研究将热力学与预催化和后催化复合物的结构联系起来，澄清了先前的实验结果，并强调了基于18-ComC的PEP肽抑制剂在变形链球菌中的设计。
